ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-clearance screening of all UBOs, directors, senior managers, authorized signatories and material family members against Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission sanctions and AML databases, Taiwan Central Bank/central authority sanctions list, Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau AML/CFT records, United Nations Security Council sanctions, and OFAC SDN List. PEP status must be determined for PRC political, military, judicial and state-enterprise office holders and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for mainland-China sourced capital, with original notarized identity documents, source-of-wealth evidence and complete wire-transfer trail required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration and One-Stop Service Portal - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Examination System (公司名稱暨所營事業預查線上申請系統, gcis.nat.gov.tw)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in Traditional Chinese characters. An English or romanized name may be used as a secondary designation but does not supersede the Chinese name. Pinyin transliteration alone is not accepted as a legal name. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must not imply a financial license or regulated activity unless the corresponding approval has been obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name and business scope pre-examination is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days from the date of service of the rejection decision. If the administrative appeal is dismissed, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit within 30 days from service of the appeal decision. An approved pre-examination may be extended once for up to 180 additional days by filing before the original 180-day validity period expires, and a fresh pre-application may be submitted if the original reservation will not be used.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a licensed multi-family office or discretionary portfolio adviser. Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission requires a physical registered office in Taiwan with substantive local management, a local compliance officer, on-site books and records, and a verifiable place of business for regulatory inspection. A virtual-office mailbox is insufficient and would not satisfy the commercial-substance requirements for an ISIC 6430 financial-services entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - estimated 85% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by Taiwan authorities during the first 12 months after licensing, and at least 60% likelihood in each subsequent year. The risk is higher because the entity is mainland-China owned, operates in a high-risk AML/CFT category, and will handle discretionary portfolio mandates for multiple private client families.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan (R.O.C.) Company Act (公司法), Articles 1, 98-101, 129, 154, 192, 387; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國人投資條例), Articles 6-10; Company Identification Number Guidelines; Securities Investment Trust and Consulting Act (For license only).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration One-Stop Portal (One Stop Company Registration & Commercial Administration System).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Application Form and Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) with Foreign Investment Approval Letter; filed via online company registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital set by Taiwan Company Act for a limited liability company; nevertheless, foreign investors must obtain an Investment Approval from MOEA Investment Commission before remitting funds, and paid-in capital must be fully deposited into a Taiwan NT$-denominated bank account and verified by a licensed CPA. No escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company be incorporated under Taiwan's Company Act and the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; the draft Articles of Incorporation are adopted; the initial paid-in capital of NT$[amount] is subscribed and shall be remitted from overseas before the filing date; the registered office located at [address] is adopted; the following officers are appointed: [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Compliance Officer; the officers and external counsel are authorized to execute all filings, tax registrations, bank account openings, and license applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Approval and Business Scope Classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce - online Name Registration System (Company and Commercial Registration Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Chinese/English company name and primary business classifications via the online portal. The name must not duplicate an existing registered company and must not contain prohibited words. No notarization is required at this stage; a provisional name approval certificate is issued automatically.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for duplication or prohibited wording, the applicant may file a re-check with up to six alternative names within the same portal pass within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval from MOEA Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Investment Commission (Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign investor's application for approval to make an outward remittance and investment in Taiwan. The application must include the company incorporation plan, capital structure, source of funds, and identity verifications. Once approved, the applicant receives a Foreign Investment Approval (FIA) letter enabling the remittance of funds and subsequent registration. This is mandatory for all non-Taiwan shareholders exceeding 5% ownership.
required_dossiers: investor passport or overseas corporate certificate of incorporation
shareholder register of the parent entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, amendments and supplemental evidence may be filed within 30 calendar days through the same application channel without reapplying from scratch; major scope changes require a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Overseas Remittance and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated banking institution (Depository Bank) and a local Taiwan CPA firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After FIA approval, open a temporary company bank account at a Taiwan bank, remit the approved foreign currency investment amount, convert into New Taiwan Dollars, and place the funds into the account. Instruct a Taiwan CPA to issue a capital verification report certifying the paid-in capital and the balance. This report is mandatory for the company registration filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If funds are delayed, file a supplemental bank remittance certificate with the CPA; the verification report date will be adjusted to the actual deposit date. Avoid using the funds before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration with MOEA (Issuance of Company Registration Certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce - One Stop Company Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application with the approved name, Articles of Incorporation, identity documents, CPA capital verification, foreign investment approval, and registered office address proof. Pay the registration fee. Obtain the company registration certificate and the Unified Business Number (UBI) assigned automatically from MOEA. The registration approval serves as the company's birth certificate.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (signed by all shareholders)
registered office lease agreement or ownership proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA issues an inquiry or correction notice, the applicant must respond within 14 calendar days. Supplementary documents can be submitted online; failure to respond within the period results in withdrawal of the application, which can be re-filed via fast-track same-day procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Labor and Commercial Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance), Bureau of Labor Insurance and local municipal office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the mandatory tax registration for the company (Unified Business Number tax registration includes VAT/business sales tax), register as a withholding tax agent and obtain a company seal/chop. File labor insurance and labor pension fund establishment with the Labor Insurance Bureau within 15 days of employment of the first employee. Apply for municipal commercial registration (if the WFOE will engage in certain retail/premises activities) and fire-safety clearance of the office if it hosts employees.
required_dossiers: lease agreement and business tax TCR form
employment agreement and employees’ insured list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authorities require clarification about the business venue (e.g. address mismatch), submit the lease certificate, utility bill in company name, and a property floor-plan diagram within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC, 金融監督管理委員會), Securities and Futures Bureau (證券期貨局)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Securities Investment Consulting Enterprise License (證券投資顧問事業許可證) under the Securities Investment Trust and Consulting Act (證券投資信託及顧問法), required for multi-family discretionary portfolio advisory work.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (formerly Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category 6 - General Office/Service Premises, no manufacturing activity; no formal EIA required).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A to office-only operations. Where applicable, wastewater discharge to municipal sewers must meet effluent standards under the Water Pollution Control Act; electronic equipment and air-conditioning are subject to the Energy Management Act, and any hazardous waste must be handled by licensed waste carriers per the Waste Disposal Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and approval under the Fire Services Act for B-2 commercial office premises; a municipal use permit (Building Use Permit) must confirm the property is zoned for financial services use; occupational safety and health clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including general safety inspection, lighting/electricity compliance, and fire evacuation planning. All required certifications must be presented on-site during the FSC license inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China (国家税务总局) – unified electronic tax bureau portal: www.chinatax.gov.cn (ETax platform, 电子税务局)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The WFOE obtains its Unified Social Credit Code (USCC, 18-digit) at incorporation from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), and for tax purposes this USCC is concurrently recognised as the taxpayer identification number (纳税人识别号). Under the 'multi-license integration' (多证合一) regime, tax registration is automatic upon issuance of the business license; within 30 days thereafter the entity must log into the provincial Dongshui electronic tax bureau to complete tax supplementary registration (涉税信息补充), including bank account details, financial software information, authorised tax agent, and industry classification. The tax authority then activates the VAT taxpayer status and issues the digital tax registration certificate electronically. No separate TIN application is required for a WFOE, but a foreign parent must hold a non-resident tax identification through the CRS/EIAs process for treaty relief applications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box mechanism or pass-through election exists in PRC law. The WFOE is mandatorily taxed as a resident legal person under the Enterprise Income Tax Law (CIT rate 25%) on its worldwide income. For VAT purposes, an entity whose annual taxable turnover is not more than CNY 5,000,000 may elect to be taxed as a small-scale taxpayer (lower rate of 1% currently available under temporary policy; normally 3%); any entity with annual taxable turnover exceeding CNY 5,000,000 must be classified as a general VAT taxpayer and file under the general method. No hybrid mismatch election is available, but CFC rules, thin capitalisation, and general anti-abuse rules apply to override mismatched structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All WFOEs must complete basic tax registration within 30 days after business license issuance, regardless of revenue. For VAT general taxpayer status, registration becomes compulsory once annual taxable turnover exceeds CNY 5,000,000. Below this threshold, the entity may remain a small-scale taxpayer (3% or 1% reduced rate) or voluntarily register as a general taxpayer if it is able to comply with accounting and invoicing requirements.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China has implemented a mandatory fully-digital electronic invoice (全电发票/数电票) system through the central electronic invoice platform (电子发票服务平台). Invoices are issued, delivered, and automatically reconciled in real time with the STA's tax digital account (税务数字账户); no physical stamping or manual clearance is used. Large issuers must integrate their ERP with the tax platform using API-based data exchange to push invoice data in real time. Legacy taxpayers continue using the Golden Tax System (金税四期) with 'UKI' taxpayer electronic key devices. The tax authorities perform automatic cross-validation of invoice data against customs declarations, FX receipts, and taxpayer profiles.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from mainland China (including exports to Taiwan region as a separate customs territory) are zero-rated for VAT, with refund of creditable input VAT. Cross-border supply of discretionary portfolio advisory and multi-family office management services to offshore clients may qualify for zero-rating only if the service is completely consumed outside mainland China and the transaction meets all conditions of STA Announcement 2016 No. 32, as amended: (1) the service recipient is a non-resident enterprise or individual; (2) the service does not relate to Chinese real estate or tangible movable property located in China; (3) the service does not involve a Chinese-resident beneficiary deriving economic gain inside China; and (4) the consideration is received from abroad (foreign exchange or offshore RMB). The WFOE must retain evidence and issue a zero-rated VAT invoice prior to filing the refund application.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (海关出口货物报关单) for physical goods exports
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Carrier's Cargo Manifest
Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate (出口收汇核销单/结汇水单 or 涉外收入申报单)
Zero-Rated VAT Invoice (增值税普通发票 at 0%)
Cross-Border Service Agreement / Statement of Work / Service Completion Certificate
Tax Residence Certificate or Non-Resident Registration Proof of the Overseas Client
Input VAT Invoice Bundle and Export Cost Ledger for Refund Calculation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported claims for export zero-rating or VAT refunds are subject to retrospective clawback of the entire refund amount plus interest under the Tax Collection and Administration Law, with a 3-year limitation period that extends to 10 years where fraud is proved. The statutory penalty ranges from 50% to 500% of the refund amount falsely obtained (Article 63). Criminal exposure arises under Articles 204 and 205 of the Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refunds or false issuance of special VAT invoices, punishable by fines, asset forfeiture, imprisonment up to life, and permanent disqualification from export VAT refund treatment. The STA's 'Golden Tax Phase IV' AI risk engine automatically flags zero-rated invoices without matching customs or FX data, triggering compulsory on-site audit, cross-border information exchange requests, and anti-money-laundering referral to the PBOC.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), with Taiwan Central Bank (CBC) and Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) exercising cross-strait remittance and banking supervision authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is fully convertible for current-account trade and cross-border service flows after bank-level transaction verification; capital-account convertibility remains controlled, requiring SAFE FDI registration, permitted investment purpose, and post-entry monitoring. Profit remittance to the Taiwan parent is permitted only after statutory audit, corporate income tax clearance, and SAFE/bank verification of dividend withholding tax. Taiwan TWD is current-account convertible, but mainland-bound capital remittances require FSC/MOEA investment approval, CBC remittance declaration, and bank confirmation; unlicensed capital transfers between the PRC WFOE and Taiwan are not freely convertible.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Neither the PRC nor Taiwan imposes a fixed mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Under SAFE, PRC export and service proceeds must be repatriated to an onshore foreign-currency or RMB account within 180 days after export declaration or service completion, supported by customs declarations, contracts, invoices, and settlement records; foreign-currency balances may be retained or converted to RMB at the reporting bank's spot rate. Taiwan requires export and cross-border service earnings to be collected within the contractual settlement term and declared to a CBC-approved bank; no forced surrender percentage applies. For the MFO's cross-border advisory fees received from Taiwan clients, current-account service receipts must be matched with the advisory agreement, fee schedule, and settlement evidence for SAFE and tax audit integrity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary treasury rails. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Payoneer, Currenxie) are not licensed as deposit-taking banks in the PRC or Taiwan and cannot hold SAFE capital-account balances, file FDI registrations, or serve as settlement banks for export/service proceeds. Rating: MEDIUM only as an ancillary collection gateway for overseas client fees, provided funds are swept into a licensed onshore account within 24 hours and the underlying advisory inflows are fully documented for SAFE, tax, and AML audit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PRC WFOE onboarding mandates physical attendance: the legal representative and seal custodian must appear at the bank branch with original incorporation documents, FDI registration filing, articles of association, board resolutions, shareholder register, and corporate seal cards; remote video onboarding is not accepted for first-time capital-escrow or basic settlement accounts. Taiwan-regulated banks also require the locally appointed director or authorized representative to attend in person; remote identification may be used for additional signatories only after the primary banking relationship is established.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate purpose includes discretionary portfolio management without a PRC financial license, creating an AML special-license red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Proof of AMAC private fund manager registration or CSRC-licensed securities investment advisory qualification; compliance undertaking documenting that the MFO provides only non-discretionary advice; client agreements restricting execution authority; external legal opinion on financial-service licensing limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait investment compliance gap due to missing FDI approval or Taiwan investment authorization.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration certificate; foreign-invested enterprise filing receipt; Taiwan FSC/MOEA mainland-investment approval; CBC remittance declaration; corporate registration with explicit WFOE capital structure; summary of investment route from Taiwan parent to PRC entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity from family trust structures and offshore SPV shareholding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organizational chart; trust deed with settlor, protector, and beneficiary layers; register of controllers; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; independent background investigation; PEP screening results; Hong Kong or other offshore registry excerpts; audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business classification (ISIC 6430, Multi-Family Office) triggering enhanced due diligence on advisory fee flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/KYC policy and procedures; designated compliance officer and money-laundering reporting officer appointment letters; client risk-rating methodology; sample engagement letters; periodic transaction-monitoring reports; regulatory license where applicable; professional-indemnity insurance certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Taiwan parent routes investment funds via CTBC Bank or Bank of China through SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's SAFE-designated FDI capital account, using remittance purpose 'Foreign Direct Investment Equity Contribution' and referencing the SAFE FDI registration code. The bank verifies the FDI registration, business license, capital-account opening notice, and source-of-funds evidence, then permits RMB settlement under SAFE settlement rules; the resulting RMB funds remain monitored in a capital-account settlement sub-ledger and may only be disbursed for documented operational purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border service fees, dividends, and advisory settlements are cleared through SWIFT MT103 or CIPS for China-Taiwan RMB payments; trade-related disbursements requiring documentary security may use Commercial Letters of Credit. Each outbound transfer is matched to the underlying contract, tax payment certificates, invoice, and SAFE current-account authenticity verification; Taiwan-side outward remittances require CBC declaration through the remitting bank and FSC compliance for amounts above the regulatory reporting threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB FX forwards executed with SAFE-designated banks under the real-exposure principle.
Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) used by the Taiwan parent for CNH/CNY treasury overlay.
Cross-currency swaps between CNY, TWD, and USD where genuine debt or investment exposure is proven.
Plain-vanilla FX options and FX swaps with licensed bank counterparties, prohibited for speculative arbitrage.
Currency-linked structured deposits only when an underlying current-account or capital-account exposure exists and the tenor complies with SAFE short-borrowing and settlement restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements Approval and Shareholders' Meeting Minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs (Taiwan); minutes retained on-site for statutory inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before June 30 for calendar-year companies (within six months of the December 31 balance-sheet date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors exposed to administrative fines of NT$10,000–NT$50,000; unapproved financial statements preclude lawful dividend declarations; persistent default may trigger compulsory deregistration by the company registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return and Final Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1–May 31 following the fiscal year-end (calendar year basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A surcharge of 3% of the underpaid tax for every two-month delay plus daily interest; tax execution and asset attachment if unpaid; misreporting may trigger criminal tax evasion liability for the responsible officer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) and Shareholding Structure Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration System (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually after the shareholders' meeting and no later than the date prescribed by the competent authority; within 15 days of any share transfer event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of NT$50,000–NT$500,000 for false or omitted UBO disclosure; repeated violation authorizes administrative strike-off and disqualification of responsible persons.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Regulatory Compliance and License Renewal Filing (FSC-regulated Multi-Family Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of fiscal year-end (April 30) or per the FSC supervisory calendar for licensed discretionary portfolio advisors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, license suspension or revocation, and prohibition from carrying on discretionary portfolio management; may also trigger winding-up orders for unlicensed conduct.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA-audited financial statements if paid-in capital reaches or exceeds NT$30 million (approximately US$1 million) under the Taiwan Company Act; regardless of size, the FSC licensing regime for discretionary portfolio advisory / multi-family office entities imposes an annual certified audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission for licensed financial enterprises; otherwise Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TIFRS / ROC GAAP) under the Business Entity Accounting Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan's Company Act requires annual beneficial-ownership declaration to the registration authority; whenever a shareholding transfer occurs, the company must update the UBO report and file the amended shareholding structure within 15 days, disclosing each controlling layer up to the ultimate natural person; the annual confirmation after the shareholders' meeting attests the current register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200–US$3,500 per year for registered office and corporate agent services in Taipei, including mail forwarding and statutory display management
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$8,000–US$18,000 per year for a CPA-certified audit of a licensed multi-family office, depending on assets under management and transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% of taxable income for a Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise. A separate 12% surtax applies to undistributed earnings retained by a company, subject to statutory exclusions and adjustments.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan generally provides no broad corporate tax holiday for a financial or portfolio-advisory business. Incentives may include qualifying R&D investment credits, smart machinery or 5G investment credits, approved innovation incentives, and deductions for qualifying employee training or development expenditure. Incentives are activity-specific, subject to approval, documentation, statutory caps, and anti-double-benefit rules. Taiwan-source dividends received by a domestic company may qualify for the inter-corporate dividend exclusion, subject to applicable conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Taiwan Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, including the annual income tax return and required schedules, filed through the Ministry of Finance electronic filing system for profit-seeking enterprises, generally accessed through the Taiwan eTax portal or the Ministry of Finance tax filing software. Financial institutions and entities subject to statutory audit, special accounting rules, or regulated financial-sector reporting may have additional schedules and filing interfaces.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with a generally applicable provisional income tax return for the first six months unless an exemption applies. Monthly withholding tax returns are separately required where the enterprise acts as a withholding agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due from 1 May through 31 May following the end of the calendar fiscal year. A company using a non-calendar fiscal year generally files within five months after fiscal year-end. The provisional return for the first half of a calendar year is generally filed during 1 September through 30 September. Payment is due by the applicable filing deadline. Extensions require a specific statutory or administrative basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, unified business number, registered address, responsible person, fiscal year, accounting period, industry classification, tax office, filing status, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan subsidiary or branch uses its Taiwan unified business number and Taiwan registration details. The foreign parent is disclosed as shareholder or head-office information, not substituted for the Taiwan taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before tax based on Taiwan statutory financial statements, with required reconciliation to the tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan entity reports its own Taiwan accounting results. A nonresident foreign enterprise reports only Taiwan-source income attributable to Taiwan activities or a Taiwan permanent establishment, unless a special withholding regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, separately taxed income, depreciation differences, provisions, entertainment expenses, donations, fines, related-party adjustments, and other statutory differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-parent expenses unless a legally supportable allocation, direct benefit, arm's-length basis, and documentary evidence establish deductibility in Taiwan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advisory fees, portfolio-management fees, performance fees, commissions, rebates, interest, foreign-exchange gains, and other business receipts, classified by source and tax treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Determine Taiwan source under the place of service performance, business activity, payer, asset, and permanent-establishment rules. Do not characterize Taiwan-performed advisory services as offshore merely because the client or bank is abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, capital gains, investment income, and related creditable or exempt amounts, with supporting acquisition, disposal, and withholding records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Taiwan rules separately to Taiwan and foreign investments. Foreign tax credits require statutory eligibility, proof of foreign tax paid, income matching, and limitation calculations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation of fixed assets, leasehold improvements, software, and qualifying intangible assets using permitted methods and useful lives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office asset charges require evidence that the asset is used for Taiwan operations and that the allocation is reasonable and not duplicative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party purchases, services, financing, royalties, guarantees, asset transfers, and other transactions, including counterparties, jurisdictions, amounts, methods, and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with the foreign parent, affiliates, controlling persons, and commonly controlled investment entities. Maintain contemporaneous support for benefit, pricing, substance, and payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses utilized or carried forward, with year-of-origin, statutory eligibility, expiration monitoring, and required financial-audit or blue-return support.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan company generally may carry losses forward for ten years only if statutory bookkeeping, filing, and audit requirements are satisfied. Losses of a foreign parent or foreign affiliate cannot be imported into the Taiwan return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, investment credits, withholding credits, and other statutory credits, supported by certificates and expenditure records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are limited to the Taiwan tax attributable to the relevant income and may require certified foreign tax documents and prescribed attachments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Minimum tax and alternative minimum tax schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of basic income under Taiwan's Income Basic Tax Act, including qualifying exempt income and specified deductions, and comparison with ordinary income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess foreign-source income, exempt income, and incentive items for basic-income inclusion. A foreign parent is not consolidated merely because it owns the Taiwan company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the 12% surtax on current-year earnings not distributed within the prescribed period, including statutory reductions, approved reinvestment, and excluded amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend repatriation planning must distinguish ordinary corporate income tax from the separate undistributed-earnings surtax. Board resolutions and payment evidence must support any distribution exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, ordinary income tax, provisional tax credit, withholding credits, foreign tax credits, basic-income tax, undistributed-earnings surtax, penalties, interest, and net payment or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all Taiwan withholding certificates and payments before claiming credits. A refund claim should be supported by bank records, books, invoices, and source-of-income analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the responsible person and, where required, accountant certification, audited financial statements, shareholder information, transfer-pricing documents, and statutory schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-language documents should be translated or summarized as required by the competent authority. The responsible person remains accountable for accuracy even where filing is delegated to an accountant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate monthly reporting of Taiwan-source payments subject to withholding, including dividends, interest, royalties, salaries, professional fees, commissions, and payments to nonresidents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File and pay by the prescribed deadline after payment or crediting. Obtain treaty or applicable relief documentation before applying a reduced rate; do not retroactively assume treaty eligibility.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual filing may result in a surcharge generally calculated as a percentage of tax payable, subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts, and a tax authority assessment based on available information. Failure to pay assessed tax generally produces a surcharge of 1% for each two-day period, subject to a statutory cap, plus interest. Late or incorrect withholding filings can create unpaid withholding tax, surcharges, interest, administrative fines, and joint liability for the withholding agent. Deliberate false reporting, concealment, omitted income, fabricated expenses, or fraudulent invoices may trigger criminal tax-evasion liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on Taiwan-source dividends paid by a Taiwan company to a nonresident company or individual, subject to an applicable tax treaty or other legally effective relief. Dividends paid to a Taiwan resident company are generally subject to Taiwan domestic inter-corporate dividend rules rather than the nonresident withholding rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Taiwan does not automatically apply a reduced rate merely because the recipient is resident in a foreign jurisdiction. Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence or equivalent documentation issued by the recipient's competent tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement, confirm the limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements where applicable, and retain contracts, payment records, ownership evidence, and substance documentation. The Taiwan payer or withholding agent applies the treaty rate only where procedural requirements are satisfied and remains responsible for withholding, reporting, and remittance. If relief is not available at payment, the recipient generally must pursue refund or adjustment procedures through the Taiwan tax authority. The cross-Strait tax arrangement with Mainland China must be checked separately for legal effectiveness, implementing rules, and current administrative practice; Mainland residence alone does not establish an automatic reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For payments to nonresidents, Taiwan domestic withholding is generally 20% on royalties and 20% on interest, subject to specific statutory classifications, financial-institution rules, approved reductions, and applicable treaty rates. Treaty rates vary by treaty and commonly reduce interest or royalty withholding to approximately 10% or another negotiated ceiling. Interest on specified Taiwan government bonds, corporate bonds, financial instruments, or approved financing arrangements may have special rates. Taiwan-source service fees are commonly subject to 20% withholding when paid to a nonresident, subject to source rules, treaty business-profit provisions, and permanent-establishment analysis. Related-party financing must also satisfy thin-capitalization, arm's-length, beneficial-owner, and substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taiwan local-file documentation generally applies where annual net revenue is at least NT$300 million or where related-party transaction thresholds are met, commonly including annual related-party purchases or sales of at least NT$200 million or other related-party transactions of at least NT$100 million, subject to the detailed transaction categories, exemptions, and current regulations. A master file is generally required for a Taiwan entity belonging to a multinational group whose consolidated annual revenue reaches at least NT$7 billion, subject to statutory exclusions and filing rules. A country-by-country report generally applies to a Taiwan constituent entity of a multinational group meeting the applicable consolidated-revenue threshold, currently generally EUR750 million or its prescribed equivalent, and related reporting conditions.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other methods permitted under Taiwan transfer-pricing regulations where the prescribed methods cannot reasonably be applied and the taxpayer demonstrates reliability and consistency
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a single UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime applicable to every holding or service company. Substance is nevertheless enforced through transfer-pricing rules, controlled foreign company rules, beneficial-ownership analysis, anti-avoidance provisions, permanent-establishment principles, foreign tax credit rules, withholding rules, and the general substance-over-form doctrine. A multi-family office must demonstrate real Taiwan functions, qualified personnel, premises, risk control, investment-advisory authority, client and mandate records, decision-making evidence, compliant custody arrangements, and arm's-length remuneration. Portfolio custody, payment execution, and regulated investment management cannot be outsourced in a manner inconsistent with FSC licensing requirements or used to disguise a passive shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing discretionary portfolio management, securities investment advice, solicitation, custody, fund management, or client-money handling in Taiwan without the required Financial Supervisory Commission authorization or through an entity whose approved business scope does not cover the activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory orders to cease business, corrective action, license denial or revocation, administrative fines under applicable securities and financial laws, disgorgement or restitution, and potential criminal liability for unauthorized securities or investment activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face administrative sanctions, disqualification, civil compensation, and criminal prosecution. Directors are not automatically liable for all corporate debts, but personal liability can arise from their own unlawful acts, knowing participation, statutory breaches, or criminal conduct. Travel restrictions may be imposed only under applicable judicial or enforcement procedures; imprisonment depends on the specific offense and conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing advisory income, understating Taiwan-source receipts, fabricating expenses, using sham service agreements, falsely claiming foreign tax credits, or manipulating residence or service-location records to avoid Taiwan tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of omitted tax, statutory surcharges, interest, administrative penalties, and criminal prosecution. Under Taiwan tax law, serious intentional evasion may result in imprisonment and criminal fines, with the exact range depending on the violated statute, amount, method, repetition, and judicial findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person, accounting personnel, and participating advisers may be prosecuted personally. Civil restitution, tax recovery from responsible persons where legally permitted, asset preservation, and restrictions on departure may follow judicial or enforcement orders. Corporate limited liability does not protect a director from liability for personal fraud or intentional tax offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting invoices for services not performed, routing payments through related entities without commercial substance, backdating contracts, or using personal expenses as deductible corporate costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of deductions and input tax credits, additional tax, fines, possible invoice-related penalties, and criminal liability for fraudulent tax or accounting conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, responsible persons, finance officers, and complicit vendors may incur joint civil exposure for loss, criminal prosecution, confiscation of proceeds, and restrictions imposed during investigation or enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive management fees, royalties, interest, or performance fees to a Taiwan entity; shifting profit to a low-tax affiliate; failing to document related-party transactions; or maintaining a policy inconsistent with functions, assets, and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority adjustment to arm's-length income, denial of deductions, additional income tax, interest, penalties for deficient documentation, withholding consequences, and possible audit expansion to other periods or jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors generally face corporate-level adjustment rather than automatic personal liability, but intentional falsification, obstruction, or participation in evasion can create personal civil and criminal exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Representing Taiwan-performed investment advice as entirely offshore, using a Taiwan office or personnel to conclude or habitually negotiate contracts for a foreign principal without disclosure, or allocating all profit to a foreign affiliate despite Taiwan personnel performing core functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of Taiwan-source income or permanent-establishment profits, corporate tax assessment, withholding tax assessment, interest, penalties, and potential treaty-abuse investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may incur personal liability for deliberate false filings or obstruction. A foreign parent may also be exposed to Taiwan tax and procedural obligations without automatically receiving the benefit of Taiwan subsidiary limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Onboarding undisclosed beneficial owners, accepting unexplained wealth, failing to identify politically exposed persons, omitting suspicious transaction reports, structuring transfers to avoid controls, or treating family-office clients as exempt from customer due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, enhanced supervision, business restrictions, license suspension or revocation, suspicious-transaction investigation, asset freezing, and criminal liability for money laundering or participation in predicate offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and senior managers may be personally prosecuted where they knowingly assist, ignore, or facilitate laundering. Confiscation, restitution, asset restraint, and judicial travel restrictions may apply; imprisonment depends on the proven offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Commingling client assets with corporate funds, receiving client investment money into an unauthorized account, allowing an adviser to control custody without authorization, or using client assets to finance affiliate operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory intervention, restitution, asset freezing, license sanctions, administrative fines, and possible criminal charges for breach of financial-sector, trust, securities, or fraud rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may be liable for restoration of client assets and damages and may face criminal prosecution for misappropriation, fraud, or unauthorized financial activity. Corporate limited liability does not shield deliberate diversion of client property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, or other Taiwan-source amounts to a foreign recipient without withholding, withholding at an unsupported treaty rate, or failing to file and remit the withheld amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the unpaid withholding tax from the withholding agent, surcharges, interest, administrative fines, denial of treaty relief, and possible criminal exposure for deliberate concealment or misuse of withheld funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company or withholding agent is primarily liable, but the responsible person and finance officers may face personal liability or prosecution for knowing non-remittance, falsification, or deliberate evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Taiwan company with nominee directors, no qualified personnel, no genuine office, no independent decision-making, or undocumented circular flows designed solely to obtain treaty access, hide beneficial ownership, or shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, tax recharacterization, disallowance of deductions, beneficial-owner and anti-avoidance adjustments, AML referrals, regulatory sanctions, and potential criminal proceedings where fraud or laundering is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and actual controlling persons may face civil claims, tax recovery, asset preservation, and criminal prosecution. Piercing the corporate veil is fact-specific and is not automatic merely because a company is foreign-owned.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Accounting, books, and record retention failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain Taiwan books, omitting bank and custody records, destroying communications, refusing lawful tax inspection, or retaining records insufficient to substantiate client mandates, expenses, related-party charges, or source of income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Estimated assessment, denial of deductions or loss carryforwards, administrative fines, audit escalation, adverse evidentiary presumptions, and separate penalties for obstruction or failure to produce records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person and accounting personnel may incur personal administrative or criminal exposure for intentional destruction, falsification, or obstruction. Departure restrictions require a lawful statutory or judicial basis and are not automatic for ordinary filing errors.
